identity.title: Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows

problem.claim: Evaluate language models on complex, real-world enterprise text-to-SQL workflows spanning heterogeneous databases, SQL dialects, and operations.

gap.claim: Traditional text-to-SQL benchmarks do not capture the long-context, metadata/code search, multi-query, and intricate reasoning demands of enterprise workflows.

contributions.claim: Introduces Spider 2.0, an evaluation framework with 632 enterprise-level text-to-SQL workflow problems derived from real data applications.
Provides databases, baseline models, and code for the benchmark.

stated_novelty.claim: The benchmark targets real-world enterprise workflows, including local or cloud databases, diverse SQL dialects, metadata and documentation search, project-codebase search, and multi-query operations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that an o1-preview-based code-agent framework solved 21.3% of Spider 2.0 tasks, versus 91.2% on Spider 1.0 and 73.0% on BIRD.
The authors report that Spider 2.0 tasks often involve databases with over 1,000 columns and SQL workflows exceeding 100 lines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Enterprise text-to-SQL involves heterogeneous data systems, dialects, and operations beyond a single query.
Spider 2.0 packages 632 workflow problems from enterprise-level use cases and real data applications.
Tasks require metadata, documentation, and codebase search, long-context processing, intricate reasoning, and multiple SQL queries.
The evaluated code-agent framework achieves substantially lower task success on Spider 2.0 than on earlier benchmarks, motivating further improvement.

source_observation.claim: The abstract specifies concrete workflow demands—database scale, search targets, context length, query multiplicity, and comparison scores—instead of describing enterprise difficulty only generally.

lessons.interpretation: A task's difficulty becomes more actionable when decomposed into observable environmental and output requirements.
lessons.application: Define a benchmark or system claim by listing required information sources, context scale, output structure, and at least one cross-benchmark comparison.
lessons.exception: Avoid cross-benchmark score comparisons when datasets, metrics, or evaluation protocols are not sufficiently comparable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify Spider 2.0's evaluation metric, task composition, or detailed comparison protocol.
The reported 21.3% result is tied to an o1-preview-based code-agent framework; performance of other models or agents is not given.
No per-capability breakdown or error analysis is provided.
